description: CLUSTER BY on CREATE TABLE through the SQL surface - the cluster_by cell of SHOW TABLES (LINEAR(keys) exactly as written, empty when unclustered): single and multiple keys, alongside COMMENT, plain columns and function/CAST/arithmetic/concat expressions, preserved by CREATE TABLE CLONE and CREATE DATABASE CLONE, schema-qualified names, the unknown-column refusal (creating nothing), and the CLUSTER BY-before-the-column-list placement Snowflake also accepts. Converted 1:1 from features/ClusterByTest (now retired).

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, region VARCHAR) CLUSTER BY (region)
CREATE TABLE orders (order_id INTEGER, customer_id INTEGER, order_date VARCHAR, status VARCHAR) CLUSTER BY (order_date, status)
CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, price INTEGER)
CREATE TABLE sales (id INTEGER, product VARCHAR, amount INTEGER) CLUSTER BY (product) COMMENT = 'Sales data clustered by product'
CREATE TABLE inventory (item_id INTEGER, category VARCHAR, quantity INTEGER) CLUSTER BY (category)
CREATE TABLE original_table (id INTEGER, region VARCHAR, data VARCHAR) CLUSTER BY (region)
CREATE TABLE users (user_id INTEGER, country VARCHAR, name VARCHAR) CLUSTER BY (country)
SHOW TABLES LIKE 'users' IN SCHEMA test_db_clone.test_schema
CREATE TABLE analytics.metrics (metric_id INTEGER, date VARCHAR, value INTEGER) CLUSTER BY (date)
SHOW TABLES LIKE 'metrics' IN SCHEMA analytics
CREATE TABLE t1 (id INTEGER, col1 VARCHAR) CLUSTER BY (col1)
CREATE TABLE t2 (id INTEGER, col2 VARCHAR, col3 VARCHAR) CLUSTER BY (col2, col3)
CREATE TABLE t3 (id INTEGER, col4 VARCHAR)
CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER, email VARCHAR, created_at VARCHAR) CLUSTER BY (UPPER(email))
CREATE TABLE events (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, timestamp VARCHAR) CLUSTER BY (UPPER(name), DATE(timestamp))
SELECT CONTAINS("cluster_by", 'UPPER(name)'), CONTAINS("cluster_by", 'DATE'), CONTAINS("cluster_by", 'timestamp') FROM TABLE(RESULT_SCAN(LAST_QUERY_ID()))
CREATE TABLE data (id INTEGER, value VARCHAR, amount DECIMAL) CLUSTER BY (CAST(value AS INTEGER))
SELECT CONTAINS("cluster_by", 'CAST'), CONTAINS("cluster_by", 'value'), CONTAINS("cluster_by", 'INTEGER') FROM TABLE(RESULT_SCAN(LAST_QUERY_ID()))
CREATE TABLE metrics (id INTEGER, value INTEGER, multiplier INTEGER) CLUSTER BY (value * multiplier)
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER, customer_id INTEGER, order_date VARCHAR, amount DECIMAL) CLUSTER BY (UPPER(order_date), customer_id + 1000)
SELECT CONTAINS("cluster_by", 'UPPER'), CONTAINS("cluster_by", 'order_date'), CONTAINS("cluster_by", 'customer_id') FROM TABLE(RESULT_SCAN(LAST_QUERY_ID()))
CREATE TABLE sales (id INTEGER, region VARCHAR, amount INTEGER, date VARCHAR) CLUSTER BY (region, UPPER(date), amount * 2)
SELECT STARTSWITH("cluster_by", 'LINEAR(region,'), CONTAINS("cluster_by", 'UPPER'), CONTAINS("cluster_by", 'amount') FROM TABLE(RESULT_SCAN(LAST_QUERY_ID()))
CREATE TABLE logs (id INTEGER, message VARCHAR, timestamp VARCHAR) CLUSTER BY (SUBSTRING(message, 1, 10))
CREATE TABLE original (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, value INTEGER) CLUSTER BY (UPPER(name), value * 10)
CREATE TABLE people (id INTEGER, first_name VARCHAR, last_name VARCHAR) CLUSTER BY (first_name || ' ' || last_name)
CREATE TABLE cbad (id INTEGER) CLUSTER BY (nosuchcol)
CREATE TABLE lead_single CLUSTER BY (i) (i INTEGER, name VARCHAR)
CREATE TABLE lead_multi CLUSTER BY (region, status) (id INTEGER, region VARCHAR, status VARCHAR)
CREATE TABLE lead_expr CLUSTER BY (UPPER(name)) (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR)
CREATE TABLE lead_data CLUSTER BY (category) (item_id INTEGER, category VARCHAR, quantity INTEGER)
